mods.description:

mods.name: Alien Worlds Framework
mods.author: maevi
mods.description:
Tired of always playing on the same boring earthlike worlds?
So am I. This is a mod framework for creating entirely new types of planets, fully integrated with Worldbuilder.

Does not include any planet types on its own, check the linked steam collection for a few official ones.

<size=24>FAQ</size>

<size=16>What can this do that Worldbuilder can't?</size>

Worldbuilder is first and foremost a map creator. A mod can define the exact tiles/settlements/etc that should be generated, but it can't easily generate custom planets on the fly. This framework allows mods to do things like:

- Restrict which biomes should generate
- Replace ocean tiles and textures, or remove oceans outright to have a fully solid world
- Change the global average temperature to anything they want
- And more!

All while keeping the vanilla world generation fully intact.
Also note that while Worldbuilder has first-class support and I fully recommend using it, the mod can also work without it. In standalone mode, which planet type to generate can be selected in the mod's settings.

<size=16>Is this compatible with X?</size>

Most likely yes. I tested it with ~1200 mods and it worked perfectly well, but if you come across something that breaks please let me know.

<size=16>How can I create a custom planet type using this?</size>

Check the source code, documentation's all there:
https://codeberg.org/maevi/rimworld-mods/src/branch/main/alien-worlds

mods.name: BiomesKit (Continued)
mods.author: Zaljerem
mods.description:
Original mod by Odeum
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2153006237
If the original author requests it, I will remove this update.

--

I am aware this is contained within ReGrowth. I am a fan of more options for everyone.  

If you run ReGrowth: Core, you don't need this mod. I don't want to explicitly set it incompatible because I suspect they could coexist, but do so at your own risk; it's really unnecessary.

--

Original mod notes (1.4):

BiomesKit is a framework for the placement of biomes on the world map at worldgen. Previously, modders needed to utilize C# to add new biomes to rimworld. With BiomesKit, placement of a biome can be controlled with XML tags in the BiomeDef itself.

With BiomesKit as a dependency, you too can make your own biomes mod with minimal hassle! Features of BiomesKit includes but are not limited to:
* Spawning biomes based on factors like elevation, rainfall, hilliness and more!
* Restricting your biome to spawn only on specific vanilla biomes, or even biomes from other mods!
* Changing the hilliness of a tile to a specific level, or even randomizing it!
* Custom world map tile graphics for your biome!

mods.name: Minerals Framework
mods.author: Zachary S. L. Foster
mods.description:
Version 0.1

NOTE: Under development. This is my first time adding mods to Steam, so I have some learning to do and I am sure things will need fixing.

An overhaul of anything mineable and the foundation for the "Minerals" collection of mods. This mod does not add any content to the game, but provides a framework for other mods to build upon. Rocks and minerals produced by this framework have the following improvements over vanilla:

- More realistic and organic appearance, supporting different sizes, number of textures, distribution of texture positions, and random scattering
- More customizable mining products, including support for multiple products, product probabilities, and product quantities
- Mining products are randomly dropped while mining instead of all at once when the rock is destroyed
- Miner skill affects amount of resources mined
- Minerals have a "size" that affects how many resources can be mined from them and their appearance
- Minerals can grow, shrink, spawn, and despawn in response to environmental conditions, such as temperature, precipitation, and light levels
- An optional "snowy" texture that appears when enough snow has accumulated nearby
- A "mining speed" property makes how easy it is to mine independent of rock hit points

See other mods in the "Minerals" collection to get the full experience:

- Minerals Rock: Complete overhaul of mountains and rocks
- Minerals Sparkle: Valuable crystals that can be mined for gems in remote and extreme biomes
- Minerals Frozen: Dynamic ice and snow that can be used for building and cooling rooms

The Minerals mods are still being balanced. Feel free to let me know if anything needs to be adjusted!

I am not aware of any incompatibilities with other mods, but please let me know if you find any.

See the source code and report issues at: https://github.com/zachary-foster/MineralsFramework

mods.name: Pick Up And Haul - Shared Storage Access
mods.description:
Do your pawns queue outside a huge single-tile storage building while only one of them actually carries anything in? Ever seen "no storage space" when the building is nowhere near full?

The reason is simple: one hauler can reserve the entire destination tile. This is barely noticeable with stockpile zones, but a Stone Cellar or another deep-storage building may hold dozens or hundreds of stacks in one tile. While the first colonist, mech, or animal is delivering an item, everyone else treats the whole storage building as occupied.

This patch allows several haulers to share the same multi-stack storage tile at once. The limit scales with its capacity: a 3-stack container allows up to 3 haulers, while larger storage allows more, up to a hard limit of 32. Ordinary shelves, stockpile cells, graves, storage priorities, routes, and item filters are not changed.

The patch also helps Pick Up And Haul build mixed trips for these buildings, allowing accepted items such as wood, steel, and meat to be carried together instead of restricting a trip to one item type.

OPTIONAL: Enable "Allow shared source stack reservations" in mod settings to let up to 10 haulers reserve separate quantities from the same oversized source stack. This is useful with OgreStack and similar mods. The option affects only storage-hauling jobs; ordinary stacks that one pawn can take completely remain exclusive. The feature is experimental and disabled by default.

OPTIONAL VEHICLE FRAMEWORK SUPPORT: Enable "Allow shared vehicle cargo loading" to let cargo loaders reserve separate quantities from the same item stack. This is a separate experimental option, disabled by default, and can be used alone or together with shared source stacks. It supports loading selected cargo into vehicles on the map; caravan gathering, passengers, refuelling and turret ammunition are excluded. Vehicle Framework is optional.

EXAMPLE: The Stone Cellar from Adaptive Primitive Storage occupies one tile but stores up to 175 stacks. With this patch, several haulers may deliver to it at the same time instead of the first one blocking the cellar for everyone else.

WHO NEEDS THIS: players using Pick Up And Haul together with single-tile storage buildings that hold multiple item stacks.

Requires Harmony and Pick Up And Haul. Tested with Adaptive Storage Framework and Adaptive Primitive Storage.

NOT NEEDED WITH HAULER'S DREAM: that mod is a complete hauling overhaul which replaces Pick Up And Haul, and it already provides shared storage access as part of its own routing. This patch is for players who want to keep using Pick Up And Haul itself.

Unofficial compatibility patch. Safe to add to or remove from an existing save between game launches.
